s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological and systemic symptoms with signs of inflammation and possible infection in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease
key_facts: 44-year-old woman
History of systemic lupus erythematosus since 2003
Cutaneous, joint, and renal involvement
Recent treatment for SLE-associated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
Presented with one-week history of progressive headache, phonophobia, high-grade fever, vomiting, and watery diarrhea
Systemic inflammatory response syndrome on admission
Nuchal rigidity without focal neurologic deficits
Laboratory studies showed hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, MCV 103 fL, eosinophils 150 cells/mm3
Cerebrospinal fluid culture grew Enterococcus gallinarum
Developed hemoptysis, bilateral patchy pulmonary infiltrates, and acute respiratory failure
Purpuric skin rash on hospital day 4

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological and systemic symptoms with signs of inflammation and possible infection in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease
key_facts: 44-year-old woman
History of systemic lupus erythematosus since 2003
Cutaneous, joint, and renal involvement
Recent treatment for SLE-associated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
Presented with one-week history of progressive headache, phonophobia, high-grade fever, vomiting, and watery diarrhea
Systemic inflammatory response syndrome on admission
Nuchal rigidity without focal neurologic deficits
Laboratory studies showed hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, MCV 103 fL, eosinophils 150 cells/mm3
Cerebrospinal fluid culture grew Enterococcus gallinarum
Developed hemoptysis, bilateral patchy pulmonary infiltrates, and acute respiratory failure
Purpuric skin rash on hospital day 4

shortlist.label: Lupus pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of SLE and recent development of hemoptysis, bilateral patchy pulmonary infiltrates, and acute respiratory failure

shortlist.label: SLE-associated vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of SLE and presence of systemic inflammatory response syndrome, nuchal rigidity, and purpuric skin rash

shortlist.label: Cryptococcal meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of headache, phonophobia, and high-grade fever, with cerebrospinal fluid culture growing Enterococcus gallinarum, although this is not the typical pathogen

shortlist.label: Infective endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: History of recent treatment for SLE-associated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura and development of systemic inflammatory response syndrome and hemoptysis

shortlist.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of systemic inflammatory response syndrome, nuchal rigidity, and purpuric skin rash, with possible renal involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's history of systemic lupus erythematosus, recent treatment for SLE-associated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, and presentation with systemic inflammatory response syndrome, nuchal rigidity, and purpuric skin rash are consistent with SLE-associated vasculitis, which can cause a wide range of symptoms including neurological and respiratory involvement.

rejected.label: Lupus pneumonitis
rejected.why: While the patient developed hemoptysis and bilateral patchy pulmonary infiltrates, the presence of Enterococcus gallinarum in the cerebrospinal fluid and the purpuric skin rash suggest a more complex condition than lupus pneumonitis alone.

rejected.label: Cryptococcal meningitis
rejected.why: The cerebrospinal fluid culture grew Enterococcus gallinarum, not Cryptococcus, making this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Infective endocarditis
rejected.why: There is no mention of cardiac involvement or positive blood cultures that would suggest infective endocarditis.

rejected.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
rejected.why: While Wegener's granulomatosis can cause similar symptoms, the patient's history of systemic lupus erythematosus and the presence of SLE-associated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura make SLE-associated vasculitis a more likely diagnosis.
